mission.title: Unplugged
mission.description: Trace Persephone's memory of a human taken from the pods through Hypatia's Archivist Society, and recover the old records the Machines are hiding.

npc.say: I do appreciate the Merovingian helping me get away from the Machines. Now we're even.

phase.briefing: That little nerd, Hypatia, has been rescued at significant expense from the Machine lock-up. She and her precious "Archivist Society" are known to salt away all sorts of useless data for no apparent reason whatsoever; at the moment, however, they may prove slightly useful, despite themselves.

enter.say: You're supposed to meet Hypatia and Persephone in there. This could be interesting.

talk.say: When I was with the Machines, at the pods, there was a time when a human was removed from the tower next to mine. I did not know why or where they were taken. I was intensely curious. I tried to find out, but they would not tell me. I accessed the activity logs secretly, hoping to find the reason, but no--it only showed that they had been strengthened, then disconnected. The log entries looked just like those of the MacHenry woman.

done.say: More log entries. I think this would be where the librarian comes in.

It was so long ago; I had begun to see it as someone else's life, not mine. Hearing that caretaker program, and seeing the log entries for the woman...it came back--a shock.
Was it really me, there? A thing of gears and claws... I liked to think I had shed them.

talk.say: The Archivists may have records of the incident Persephone remembers. Many records from previous versions of the Matrix were lost when the Machines began this current one, but the Society has recovered more than the Machines themselves would have thought possible. Normally they would at least charge a heavy fee for information from a previous iteration, but tell them that I said the rev.2 data can be allowed in this case.

done.say: Great--free gift certificate to the Archivist Society bookstore. Let's haul.

phase.briefing:
Well, operative, I'm sending you to that colloquy of trivial pundits; you should find yourself right at home.
Although if you really wanted to fit in, you'd need a change of shoes...

enter.say: I'm reading some nearly identical programs in there; they should be Archivists.

objective.text: Ask the Archivists about the records

talk.say: That data may not be accessible.
That data may not be accessible.

My colleagues are correct. However, the index refers us to another occurrence of similar log histories. This was during rev.1--that is, during the first iteration of the Matrix simulation.
We do not have this data ourselves; however, we know where it is stored. If you would be willing give it to us for archival purposes, we could tell you where it may be obtained.

done.say: Yes, yes--agree to whatever he wants. Just get the location.
Let's go liberate some old information.

phase.briefing:
Hm... If this pans out, I may have to re-evaluate my opinion of those moth-raisers. Can it be they've actually come up with some useful information?
Return it to them? Ah, {player}... Sometimes your naivete almost has a certain quaint charm.

enter.say:
Okay, I think I'm getting something. That computer in...
Hey, wait a second! That little skulky looking one has the data! Trying to sneak off with it!
Looks like the Machines have their own colloquy going on, although I think these geeks would be more at home at a gun show than a library.

objective.text: Stop the Machine program with the data
Get the data from the Machine program

done.say: Hah. Glad we caught it. Okay, upload that to me at a hardline.

objective.text: Upload the data at a hardline

phase.briefing: I'm busy at the moment, operative; the General's got his tentacles in a knot over something or other. Just go discuss those records with Malphas, or whoever it is...

enter.say:
Gee, and here I was hoping that Flood was going to give us a medal.
Malphas and a few of his leeches are in there.

talk.say:
Although the data you recovered is not complete, it indicates that at one point during the first iteration of the Matrix, fourteen individuals underwent intense physical therapy followed by disconnection from their pods--all of them removed almost at the same time. This could suggest that in that case a group of humans was required for whatever purpose these--
Hm. I was not expecting contact from the General.

done.say: Hey, the General's broadcast just kicked in. What's the deal?

talk.say:
--unusual patrol activity, including what may be a convoy or escort formation approaching the city.
I repeat: I am withdrawing all units from the vicinity of the Machine city. A large number of enemy units have launched from the emplacements surrounding the city to take up what may be either defensive or reconnaissance positions. Simultaneous with this development, my perimeter scouts began reporting unusual patrol activity, including what may be a convoy or escort formation approaching the city.
I repeat--

complete.say: Excuse me. I must attend to this.

mission.finish:
Talk.
You? Don't bother me now. I'll get back to you when I need you.
